Rush.Name: Rush
Rush.Description:
When a creature takes the Rush main action, they move up to their speed in a straight line without jumping, then make a @UUID[Compendium.draw-steel.abilities.Item.wU69Y06G9lYFrvp6]{melee free strike} against a target when they end their move. If the creature has an ability with the Rush keyword, they can use that ability against the target instead of a free strike.

A creature can’t move through difficult terrain or shift when they rush. They can fly or burrow as part of the Rush main action if they have that movement available to them — thrusters, grav rigs, and tunneling gear included — but they can’t climb or swim while rushing unless they can automatically use that movement at full speed.

TakeCover.Name: Take Cover
TakeCover.Description: When a creature takes the [[/apply TYggdI2Kwa302NjW]]{Take Cover main action}, they get low behind whatever the street offers — an engine block, a dumpster, a doorframe — and ability rolls made against them have a double bane until the start of their next turn. Additionally, you have a double edge on tests when called for to resist environmental effects or a creature’s traits or abilities. A creature gains no benefit from this action while another creature is taunted by them.
TakeCover.EffectDescription: Ability rolls made against you have a double bane until the start of your next turn. You have a double edge on tests when called for to resist environmental effects or a creature’s traits or abilities. You gain no benefit from this while another creature is taunted by you.

PatchUp.Name: Patch Up
PatchUp.Description: A creature who uses the Patch Up main action slaps on a trauma patch, jabs a stim, or talks an adjacent creature through the pain to keep them in the fight. The target creature can spend a Recovery to regain Stamina, or can make a saving throw against one effect they are suffering that is ended by a saving throw.

SpotTarget.Name: Spot Target
SpotTarget.Description: Choose an enemy adjacent to you and tag it for your crew — a callout, a laser dot, a ping on the shared feed. The next ability power roll an ally makes against that creature before the start of your next turn has an edge.

Drive.Name: Drive
Drive.Description: A creature can take the Drive move action only while piloting a vehicle. When a creature takes the Drive move action, they cause their vehicle to move up to the vehicle’s speed, taking the driver and any passengers with it. Alternatively, a creature can use the Drive move action to have their vehicle use the Disengage move action as a free triggered action. A creature can use the Drive move action only once per round. A vehicle can only have this move action applied to it once per round. This movement can be broken up with the driver’s maneuver and main action however they wish.

Grade: Standard · Location: Head / Neural · Body Integrity: 1 · Price: ¥500 · Availability: Street

Class.Name: Operator
Class.Description:
You are an Operator — a street samurai, edgerunner, or professional shooter who fights with chrome, discipline, and a body wired to run hotter than anyone else on the field. You don’t hack the Wired and you don’t burn magic; you close distance, put rounds and blades where they count, and keep coming back for more when everyone else would already be down.

Whether you’re a Corp-Milspec asset running fire-team doctrine, a Merc carrying two kits into every job, or a Street-vet who survived the gutter long enough to become a professional, your identity is the same: chrome-forward, casts nothing, and dangerous specifically because you do not stop.

Core characteristics: Physique, Reflex · Heroic resource: Adrenaline · Starting Stamina: 21 (+9 per level) · Recoveries: 10 · Kit: yes (Merc carries two).

Adrenaline.Name: Adrenaline
Adrenaline.Description:
Adrenaline in Combat. At the start of a combat encounter (or any other tense situation the Director tracks in combat rounds), you gain Adrenaline equal to your Victories. At the start of each of your turns during combat, you gain 1d3 Adrenaline. Additionally, the first time each combat round that you take damage, you gain 1 Adrenaline. The first time you become winded or are dying in an encounter, you gain 1d3 Adrenaline. You lose any remaining Adrenaline at the end of the encounter.

Adrenaline Outside of Combat. You can’t gain Adrenaline outside of combat, but you can still use your heroic abilities and effects that cost Adrenaline without spending it. Whenever you use an ability or effect outside of combat that costs Adrenaline, you can’t use that same ability or effect outside of combat again until you earn 1 or more Victories or finish a respite. When you use an ability outside of combat that lets you spend unlimited Adrenaline on its effect, you can use it as if you had spent an amount of Adrenaline equal to your Victories.

Growing Adrenaline. You gain certain benefits in combat based on the amount of Adrenaline you currently have (see your Origin’s Growing Adrenaline table). These benefits last until the end of your turn, even if a benefit would become unavailable because you spent Adrenaline during that turn.

You automatically sense whether any creature within 10 squares has damage immunity or damage weakness to acid, cold, corruption, fire, lightning, poison, or sonic damage, learning whether they have immunity or weakness, its value, and the damage type. Additionally, you automatically sense any source of one of those damage types within 10 squares, such as a fire, a live cable, or a chemical spill.

VeteranOfTheSprawl.Name: Veteran of the Sprawl
VeteranOfTheSprawl.Description: You passively detect security systems, drones, and Corp-Milspec presence within 1 mile, and you read corp and gang signal traffic fluently. Treat your Renown as 1 higher with corp and gang contacts. The first time a Corp-Milspec operative becomes aware of you, they are frightened of you until the end of the encounter if they have Persona lower than your average potency.

BreachPoint.Name: Breach Point
BreachPoint.Description:
A breach point is a standing, reusable tear you personally open between the physical world and the deep network — a hidden, secured layer of the Wired reachable only through a breach point and anchored on your end to a live relay node (a node you or an ally has set up and is actively maintaining; see Ghost of the Sprawl).

As a main action, touch a live relay node to open a breach point into the deep network. You can then spend a main action to route yourself and any willing creatures within 10 squares of you through the breach onto a secured safehouse node, or to route back the same way. You can maintain a number of breach points equal to your Physique score, and every breach point you hold leads to the same safehouse node. If a breach point is destroyed, it drops out of your network; you can remove one voluntarily at any distance, no action required. Exploring the deep network beyond your safehouse node is possible, but safety there isn’t guaranteed.

CombatForm.Name: Combat Form
CombatForm.Description:
Your chrome and nervous system show the strain of how hot you run. Whenever you show strong emotion or increase your Adrenaline, your chrome flares — heat shimmer, static, or a visible glow in your implants.

Additionally, if you are a Corp-Milspec or Merc, you have immunity to acid, cold, corruption, fire, lightning, poison, and sonic damage equal to [[lookup @M]]{your Physique score}. If you are a Street-vet, you have immunity to your loadout damage type equal to [[lookup 2*@M evaluate=true]]{twice your Physique score}.

GrowingAdrenalineII.Description: Your Growing Adrenaline feature provides additional benefits when you have 10 or more Adrenaline.

GhostOfTheSprawl.Name: Ghost of the Sprawl
GhostOfTheSprawl.Description: As a respite activity, you establish a temporary secured relay node that lasts 24 hours. You can use it with your Breach Point feature to open a breach point into the deep network; if you do, the relay node persists as long as you maintain that breach point.

WarzoneIncarnate.Name: Warzone Incarnate
WarzoneIncarnate.Description:
You’ve walked through every kind of fire the Sprawl can throw. If you are a Corp-Milspec or Merc, you have immunity to acid, cold, corruption, fire, lightning, poison, and sonic damage equal to [[lookup 2*@M evaluate=true]]{twice your Physique score}. If you are a Street-vet, your immunity to your loadout damage type increases to [[lookup 3*@M evaluate=true]]{three times your Physique score}.

When any creature whose abilities deal acid, cold, corruption, fire, lightning, poison, or sonic damage first becomes aware of you in combat, if they have [[potency P strong]], they are [[/apply frightened save]].

Additionally, when you use Precision Strike, you can spend up to 3 Adrenaline, [[/surge 1]]{gaining 1 surge} per Adrenaline spent to use for that strike.
WarzoneIncarnate.Director: This feature is an upgrade of the effects granted by the 7th level feature “Combat Form.” You can increase the values of the effect you already have to match the values of this feature.

GrowingAdrenalineIII.Name: Growing Adrenaline III
GrowingAdrenalineIII.Description: Your Growing Adrenaline feature provides additional benefits when you have 12 or more Adrenaline.

PeakAdrenaline.Name: Peak Adrenaline
PeakAdrenaline.Description: The first time you take damage each combat round, you gain 3 Adrenaline instead of 2.

OperatorMastery.Name: Operator Mastery
OperatorMastery.Description: You gain an epic resource called Overclock. Each time you finish a respite, you gain Overclock equal to the XP you gain. You can spend Overclock on your abilities as if it were Adrenaline. You can also spend any amount of Overclock as a free maneuver to end one effect on you per Overclock spent, and you can spend 3 Overclock to open a breach point into the deep network without needing a live relay node. Overclock remains until you spend it.

CorpMilspec.Name: Corp-Milspec
CorpMilspec.Description:
“Company Asset.” Fire-team doctrine drilled into you by a corporate or military program: breaching, controlling space, and hitting hard enough to move people.

At 1st level you gain the Command skill and choose one Kit.

BreachingForce.Name: Breaching Force
BreachingForce.Description:
Whenever you damage an object with a weapon strike, the strike deals extra damage equal to [[lookup @M]]{your Physique score}. Additionally, whenever you push another creature into an object, the creature takes extra damage equal to [[lookup @M]]{your Physique score}.

As your Adrenaline grows, you gain benefits as noted on the @UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.classes.Item.3t5oRaCIWuHaazPt]{Corp-Milspec Growing Adrenaline} table. Benefits are cumulative except where an improved benefit replaces a lesser benefit.

GrowingAdrenalineCorpMilspec.Name: Growing Adrenaline
GrowingAdrenalineCorpMilspec.Description:
You gain certain benefits in combat based on the amount of Adrenaline you have. These benefits last until the end of your turn, even if a benefit would become unavailable to you because of the amount of Adrenaline you spend during your turn. Some Growing Adrenaline benefits can be applied only if you are a specific level or higher, with the level of those benefits noted in the various Growing Adrenaline tables in this section.

Adrenaline

Benefit

2

Whenever you use the Knockback maneuver, the forced movement distance gains a bonus equal to [[lookup @M]]{your Physique score}.

4

The first time you push a creature on a turn, you [[/surge 1]].

6

You gain an edge on Physique tests and the Knockback maneuver

8 (4th Level)

The first time you push a creature on a turn, you [[/surge 2]].

10 (7th Level)

You have a double edge on Physique tests and the Knockback maneuver.

12 (10th Level)

Whenever you use a heroic ability, you gain [[/heal 10 temporary]]. Additionally, whenever you make a power roll that imposes forced movement on a target, the forced movement distance gains a bonus equal to [[lookup @M]]{your Physique score}.

KineticRedirect.Name: Kinetic Redirect
KineticRedirect.Story: You redirect the energy of motion.
KineticRedirect.Trigger: The target would be force moved
KineticRedirect.Effect_spend00000000000: The forced movement distance gains a bonus equal to twice your Physique score instead.
KineticRedirect.Effect_before0000000000: You can select a new target of the same size or smaller within distance to be force moved instead. You become the source of the forced movement, determine the new target’s destination, and can push the target instead of using the original forced movement type. Additionally, the forced movement distance gains a bonus equal to [[lookup @M]]{your Physique score}.

BreachCharge.Name: Breach Charge
BreachCharge.Description: Whenever you use the @UUID[Compendium.draw-steel.abilities.Item.wNqJWJbgAbnJBqZf]{Charge} main action, you can use a strike signature ability or a strike heroic ability instead of a free strike. Additionally, you can jump as part of your charge.

DangerClose.Name: Danger Close
DangerClose.Effect_before0000000000: You vertically push the target up to 4 squares. This forced movement ignores the target’s stability, and the target takes no damage from colliding with creatures or objects. At the end of this movement, the target can make a free strike that deals extra damage equal to [[lookup @M]]{your Physique score}.

DemolitionSwing.Name: Demolition Swing
DemolitionSwing.Story: It’s easier to destroy than to create. Much easier, in fact!
DemolitionSwing.Effect_before0000000000:
You move up to your speed in a straight line. During this movement, you can move through mundane structures, including walls, which are difficult terrain for you. You automatically destroy each square of structure you move through and leave behind a square of difficult terrain.

Additionally, you make one power roll that targets each enemy you move adjacent to during this movement.

AnchoredStance.Name: Anchored Stance
AnchoredStance.Description:
You add your level to your effective size for the purpose of interacting with creatures and objects, including determining whether you can lift an object, are affected by forced movement, and so forth. This has no effect on whether you can be grabbed.

Additionally, you have a bonus to stability equal to [[lookup @M]]{your Physique score}.

JumpRig.Name: Jump Rig
JumpRig.Description: Your jump distance and height double. Additionally, when you fall, you reduce the effective height of your fall by a number of squares equal to your jump distance for the purpose of determining damage and whether you land prone. You are not prone after falling and landing on another creature.

OrbitalDrop.Name: Orbital Drop
OrbitalDrop.Story: You leap and crash down, causing a shockwave that devastates foes.
OrbitalDrop.Effect_before0000000000: You jump up to your maximum jump distance and make one power roll that targets each creature adjacent to the space where you land.

ConcussiveThrow.Name: Concussive Throw
ConcussiveThrow.Story: You strike an enemy hard enough to be a projectile that knocks a crowd of creatures around.
ConcussiveThrow.Effect_after00000000000: When the target ends this forced movement, each creature within 2 squares of the target is pushed 3 squares.

OverpoweringBuild.Name: Overpowering Build
OverpoweringBuild.Description: Your strength is unmatched. Whenever you make a Physique test, you can roll three dice and choose which two to use. Additionally, whenever you use the Knockback maneuver, the forced movement distance gains a bonus equal to [[lookup @M]]{your Physique score}.

FireForEffect.Name: Fire For Effect
FireForEffect.Story: You use your weapon to create a destructive shockwave.
FireForEffect.Effect_after00000000000: If this forced movement causes a target to be hurled through an object, that target takes an extra [[/damage 10]].

GravityWellCharge.Name: Gravity Well Charge
GravityWellCharge.Story: A shaped gravitic charge detonates and drags everyone toward you.
GravityWellCharge.Effect_after00000000000: If this forced movement causes a target to slam into you, you take no damage from the collision and the target takes the damage you would have taken.

Merc.Name: Merc
Merc.Description:
“Free Company Veteran.” Field Arsenal training — the only Origin that maintains two Kits at once — built on staying a step ahead of the job and the people paying for it.

At 1st level you gain the Demolitions skill and choose two Kits. With two Kits, you use the better Stamina, speed, stability, disengage, and distance bonus of the two, and the damage bonus of your preferred Kit (mark it on the sheet).

CombatInstinct.Name: Combat Instinct
CombatInstinct.Description:
You are never surprised. Additionally, whenever you would push a target with forced movement, you can slide them instead.

As your Adrenaline grows, you gain benefits as noted on the @UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.classes.Item.ieGJV4l66nywzuxo]{Merc Growing Adrenaline} table. Benefits are cumulative except where an improved benefit replaces a lesser benefit.

GrowingAdrenalineMerc.Name: Growing Adrenaline
GrowingAdrenalineMerc.Description:
You gain certain benefits in combat based on the amount of Adrenaline you have. These benefits last until the end of your turn, even if a benefit would become unavailable to you because of the amount of Adrenaline you spend during your turn. Some Growing Adrenaline benefits can be applied only if you are a specific level or higher, with the level of those benefits noted in the various Growing Adrenaline tables in this section.

WiredReflexes.Name: Wired Reflexes
WiredReflexes.Story: You are as elusive as a hummingbird.
WiredReflexes.Effect_spend00000000000: If the damage has any potency effects associated with it, the potency is reduced by 1 for you.
WiredReflexes.Effect_before0000000000: You take half the damage from the triggering effect and can shift up to a number of squares equal to [[lookup @A]]{your Reflex score}.

RunAndGun.Name: Run and Gun
RunAndGun.Description: You have a bonus to speed equal to [[lookup @A]]{your Reflex score}, and you ignore difficult terrain.

SuppressionKill.Name: Suppression Kill
SuppressionKill.Story: Your controlled violence strikes terror into everyone watching.

FormationBreaker.Name: Formation Breaker
FormationBreaker.Story: Organizing your forces like feckless creatures of Law. Pitiful.
FormationBreaker.Effect_before0000000000: You shift up to your speed and make one power roll that targets up to three enemies you move adjacent to during this shift.

ReadTheMark.Name: Read the Mark
ReadTheMark.Description: You have a double edge on tests made to search for hidden creatures, discern hidden motives, or detect lies. You also have a double edge on tests made to gamble!

SlipTheCuffs.Name: Slip the Cuffs
SlipTheCuffs.Description: At the start of your turn, you can end any restrained condition on you. Additionally, you have a double edge on tests made to escape being confined or imprisoned.

ContractFulfilled.Name: Contract Fulfilled
ContractFulfilled.Story: Once the first target drops, you get efficient — every kill is a chance to line up the next.
ContractFulfilled.Trigger: You reduce a creature to 0 Stamina with a strike.
ContractFulfilled.Effect_before0000000000: You target a creature adjacent to you with the same strike, using the same power roll as the triggering strike.

BreachTheLine.Name: Breach the Line
BreachTheLine.Story: You break through the enemy lines to make an example.
BreachTheLine.Effect_after00000000000: If a target who is not a leader or solo creature is winded by this strike, they are reduced to 0 Stamina and you choose an enemy within 5 squares of you. If that enemy has [[potency P average]], they are [[/apply frightened save]].

AlwaysMoving.Name: Always Moving
AlwaysMoving.Description: You move with legendary grace. Whenever you make an Reflex test, you can roll three dice and choose which two to use. Additionally, whenever you use the Disengage move action, the distance you can shift gains a bonus equal to [[lookup @A]]{your Reflex score}.

TargetMarked.Name: Target Marked
TargetMarked.Story: You attune the target to be weaker to a specific element.
TargetMarked.Effect_after00000000000:
Choose acid, cold, corruption, fire, lightning, poison, or sonic damage. The target loses any damage immunity to the chosen type and gains weakness 10 to the chosen type (save ends).

ShockAndAwe.Name: Shock and Awe
ShockAndAwe.Story: You shock your foes with the brutality of your strike, resetting the balance of combat.
ShockAndAwe.Effect_after00000000000: Each enemy within 5 squares of you is distracted until the end of the round. While a creature is distracted this way, they can’t take triggered actions or free triggered actions, ability rolls made against them gain an edge, and their characteristic scores are considered 1 lower for the purpose of resisting potencies.

StreetVet.Name: Street-vet
StreetVet.Description:
“Self-Made Killer.” Gutter Instinct training — you survived the street long enough to turn it into a profession, and you can’t be caught flat-footed.

At 1st level you gain the Intimidation skill and choose one Kit.

Loadout damage type. At 1st level, choose the rounds and rigs you favor: cryo (cold), toxin (corruption), incendiary (fire), or shock (lightning). Street-vet abilities and features that refer to your loadout damage type use this type. You can change it when you finish a respite.

GutterInstinct.Name: Gutter Instinct
GutterInstinct.Description: You can’t be surprised. Once per encounter when you are hit by a strike, you can turn that hit into a glancing blow: you take half the damage (round down) and gain 1 Adrenaline.

OverclockNerves.Name: Overclock Nerves
OverclockNerves.Story: In your anger, you revert to a more bestial form.
OverclockNerves.Trigger: You lose Stamina and are not dying.
OverclockNerves.Effect_spend00000000000: if you are not dying, you can spend a Recovery.
OverclockNerves.Effect_before0000000000: You gain [[/heal @M temp]]{temporary Stamina} equal to your Physique score as your nerves overclock and pain stops registering.

SurvivorsNose.Name: Survivor’s Nose
SurvivorsNose.Description: You gain an edge on tests made using the Survival skill.

DirtyFighting.Name: Dirty Fighting
DirtyFighting.Description: At the end of each of your turns, each enemy adjacent to you takes [[/damage @M]]{damage} equal to your Physique score.

DownTheAlley.Name: Down the Alley
DownTheAlley.Effect_after00000000000: The target can’t be hidden from you for 24 hours. Until the end of the encounter, whenever the target willingly moves, you can use a free triggered action to move.

KillerRep.Name: Killer Rep
KillerRep.Story: Your reputation hits before you do, and your opening burst staggers them.
KillerRep.Effect_after00000000000: This ability deals your loadout damage type.

StreetNetwork.Name: Street Network
StreetNetwork.Description: You can talk your way to information from gangers, fixers, and street contacts, and you automatically sense the presence of any such contact within 10 squares of you, even if they’re hidden. When negotiating with a ganger, fixer, or street contact, treat your Renown as 1 higher than usual.

Weathered.Name: Weathered
Weathered.Description: You and each ally within 5 squares of you ignore banes and other negative effects from urban and industrial hazards — toxic fumes, structural collapse, crossfire, and similar. Once per respite, you can call in a favor from a street contact to gain the benefit of a skill of your choice from the exploration group for one scene.

AmbushRush.Name: Ambush Rush
AmbushRush.Story: You strike at the target like the ultimate predator you are.
AmbushRush.Effect_after00000000000: You can shift up to 4 squares, bringing the target with you. While grabbed this way, the target takes [[/damage 2*@M]]{damage} equal to twice your Physique score at the start of each of your turns .

Crossfire.Name: Crossfire
Crossfire.Story: You set up interlocking fields of fire and a grav-lift field for your crew.
Crossfire.Effect_after00000000000:
Until the end of the encounter or until you are dying, each enemy target takes damage of your loadout damage type equal to [[/damage 2*@M type=cold/fire/corruption/lightning]]{twice your Physique score} at the end of each of your turns.

Additionally, you can [[/apply t7CYKliC6xtRG9gk]] (fly, using the grav-lift field) while the aura is active. Each ally target who starts or ends their turn in the area can also [[/apply t7CYKliC6xtRG9gk]] until the start of their next turn or until the effect ends.

Special: When you use this ability outside of combat without spending Adrenaline, you must spend 1 uninterrupted minute setting up the field, and you take [[/damage 1d6]] damage before the ability takes effect. The field lasts for 1 hour or until a combat encounter begins.

GhostOfTheGutter.Name: Ghost of the Gutter
GhostOfTheGutter.Description: You can use any Kit. During a respite, you can swap your Kit and still take another respite activity. Street Network’s sense range extends to 1 mile. Whenever you make a test to track another creature, roll three dice and choose which two to use.

LastWord.Name: Last Word
LastWord.Story: You unleash an otherworldly cry that rips through your enemies, killing the weakest of them.

SaturationFire.Name: Saturation Fire
SaturationFire.Story: You empty everything you’re carrying into the kill zone.
SaturationFire.Effect_after00000000000: This ability deals your loadout damage type and ignores damage immunity.

GrowingAdrenalineStreetVet.Name: Growing Adrenaline
GrowingAdrenalineStreetVet.Description:
You gain certain benefits in combat based on the amount of Adrenaline you have. These benefits last until the end of your turn, even if a benefit would become unavailable to you because of the amount of Adrenaline you spend during your turn. UndercityBarrens.Name: Undercity Barrens
UndercityBarrens.Description:
You grew up below the city’s foundations — flooded transit tunnels, collapsed arcades, and squatter blocks the corps wrote off decades ago. Down there you learned who runs each tunnel and how to move without being noticed.

Skills: you gain Stealth, and choose one of Streetwise, Survival, Perception, or Athletics. Skills you already have are left out of the picker; if too few remain, it also offers other skills from the same Ghostwire groups.

Your community: you know the Undercity’s squatter blocks, tunnel gangs, and scavenger crews. You have an edge on tests to recall lore about that community or to find and influence people within it (Director’s call on when it applies).

CorpArcology.Name: Corp Arcology
CorpArcology.Description:
You were raised inside a megacorp arcology — company school, company clinic, company everything. You know how departments really work and how to talk your way up a chain of command.

Skills: you gain Corporate, and choose one of Persuasion, Negotiation, Insight, or Security Systems. Skills you already have are left out of the picker; if too few remain, it also offers other skills from the same Ghostwire groups.

Your community: you know your arcology’s departments, company families, and internal security. You have an edge on tests to recall lore about that community or to find and influence people within it (Director’s call on when it applies).

SprawlDistrict.Name: Sprawl District
SprawlDistrict.Description:
You came up in the endless mid-city Sprawl, where every block has its own fixer, its own gang tax, and its own price for everything. You learned to haggle before you learned to read.

Skills: you gain Streetwise, and choose one of Negotiation, Contacts, Perception, or Brawl. Skills you already have are left out of the picker; if too few remain, it also offers other skills from the same Ghostwire groups.

Your community: you know your district’s street vendors, fixers, block associations, and local gangs. You have an edge on tests to recall lore about that community or to find and influence people within it (Director’s call on when it applies).

TransitHub.Name: Transit Hub / Freeport
TransitHub.Description:
You grew up where everything moves: a maglev terminus, a cargo freeport, or an orbital elevator’s base. Everyone passes through, everyone owes someone, and you know every route in and out.

Skills: you gain Navigation, and choose one of Contacts, Driving, Piloting, or Negotiation. Skills you already have are left out of the picker; if too few remain, it also offers other skills from the same Ghostwire groups.

Your community: you know dockworkers, freight crews, customs brokers, and travelers passing through your hub. You have an edge on tests to recall lore about that community or to find and influence people within it (Director’s call on when it applies).

OutlandWastes.Name: Outland Wastes
OutlandWastes.Description:
You’re from beyond the city walls — dead farmland, toxic scrub, and nomad convoys between ruined towns. You’re hard to kill and you know how to keep going when the water runs out.

Skills: you gain Survival, and choose one of Athletics, Driving, Perception, or Firearms. Skills you already have are left out of the picker; if too few remain, it also offers other skills from the same Ghostwire groups.

Your community: you know Outland nomad clans, convoy runners, and wasteland settlements. You have an edge on tests to recall lore about that community or to find and influence people within it (Director’s call on when it applies).

AcademicSpire.Name: Academic Spire
AcademicSpire.Description:
You were raised among a university or research spire’s archives and restricted stacks, where old histories and older forbidden texts sit side by side. You learned what the official record leaves out.

Skills: you gain History, and choose one of Occult, Matrix Theory, Medicine Lore, or Xenology. Skills you already have are left out of the picker; if too few remain, it also offers other skills from the same Ghostwire groups.

Your community: you know your spire’s faculty, archivists, research departments, and rival scholars. You have an edge on tests to recall lore about that community or to find and influence people within it (Director’s call on when it applies).

FaithDistrict.Name: Faith District
FaithDistrict.Description:
You grew up in the shadow of a cathedral of the Light — shelters, soup lines, confessionals, and street preachers. You learned the dogma, and you learned to read the desperate people who came looking for it.

Skills: you gain Religion, and choose one of Insight, Occult, Warding, or Medicine. Skills you already have are left out of the picker; if too few remain, it also offers other skills from the same Ghostwire groups.

Your community: you know the district’s churches, shelters, orders of the Light, and the faithful who depend on them. You have an edge on tests to recall lore about that community or to find and influence people within it (Director’s call on when it applies).

IndustrialDeep.Name: Industrial Deep
IndustrialDeep.Description:
You come from the foundries, mines, and reactor levels under the city — Corran labor towns most often, but open to anyone who grew up on shift work. You can keep any machine running with scrap and stubbornness.

Skills: you gain Engineering, and choose one of Repair, Athletics, Demolitions, or Electronics. Skills you already have are left out of the picker; if too few remain, it also offers other skills from the same Ghostwire groups.

Your community: you know foundry crews, labor unions, and Industrial Deep shift towns. You have an edge on tests to recall lore about that community or to find and influence people within it (Director’s call on when it applies).

WageSlave.Name: Wage-Slave
WageSlave.Description:
You worked a corporate desk job — cubicle hives, quarterly targets, and contracts you weren’t allowed to read. You know the system from the bottom and how to bargain your way through it.

Skills: you gain Negotiation, and choose two of Corporate, Persuasion, Insight, or Electronics. Skills you already have are left out of the picker; if too few remain, it also offers other skills from the same Ghostwire groups.

Starting resources: no Renown or ¥ from the Profession itself. A Director may grant a small ¥ bonus (for example ¥500) as liquid cash — never as skills, perks, or other character-power budget.

StreetDoc.Name: Street Doc
StreetDoc.Description:
You patched up people who couldn’t go to a real clinic: gunshot wounds, back-alley chrome, and overdoses, no questions asked. You learned to read a patient who’s lying about how they got hurt.

Skills: you gain Medicine, and choose two of Cybertech, Insight, Streetwise, or Medicine Lore. Skills you already have are left out of the picker; if too few remain, it also offers other skills from the same Ghostwire groups.

Starting resources: no Renown or ¥ from the Profession itself. A Director may grant a small ¥ bonus (for example ¥500) as liquid cash — never as skills, perks, or other character-power budget.

Fixer.Name: Fixer
Fixer.Description:
You connected people who needed things done with people who could do them, and took your cut. Your commlink is the most valuable thing you own.

Skills: you gain Contacts, and choose two of Negotiation, Streetwise, Insight, or Deception. Skills you already have are left out of the picker; if too few remain, it also offers other skills from the same Ghostwire groups.

Starting resources: no Renown or ¥ from the Profession itself. A Director may grant a small ¥ bonus (for example ¥500) as liquid cash — never as skills, perks, or other character-power budget.

Courier.Name: Courier
Courier.Description:
You moved packages that couldn’t go through the mail — data chips, cash, sometimes things that were still breathing. Fast, quiet, and never late.

Skills: you gain Driving, and choose two of Stealth, Navigation, Athletics, or Streetwise. Skills you already have are left out of the picker; if too few remain, it also offers other skills from the same Ghostwire groups.

Starting resources: no Renown or ¥ from the Profession itself. A Director may grant a small ¥ bonus (for example ¥500) as liquid cash — never as skills, perks, or other character-power budget.

GangSoldier.Name: Gang Soldier
GangSoldier.Description:
You held a corner for a gang: collecting protection money, running off rivals, and shooting when talking stopped working.

Skills: you gain Firearms, and choose two of Intimidation, Streetwise, Brawl, or Melee. Skills you already have are left out of the picker; if too few remain, it also offers other skills from the same Ghostwire groups.

Starting resources: no Renown or ¥ from the Profession itself. A Director may grant a small ¥ bonus (for example ¥500) as liquid cash — never as skills, perks, or other character-power budget.

SecurityGuard.Name: Security Guard
SecurityGuard.Description:
You stood post for a corp, a mall, or a private security contractor. Long hours watching cameras and doorways taught you to spot trouble before it starts.

Skills: you gain Perception, and choose two of Firearms, Intimidation, Security Systems, or Brawl. Skills you already have are left out of the picker; if too few remain, it also offers other skills from the same Ghostwire groups.

Starting resources: no Renown or ¥ from the Profession itself. A Director may grant a small ¥ bonus (for example ¥500) as liquid cash — never as skills, perks, or other character-power budget.

Smuggler.Name: Smuggler
Smuggler.Description:
You moved contraband past checkpoints and scanners — bypassing seals, forging manifests, and knowing which inspector could be paid.

Skills: you gain Security Systems, and choose two of Deception, Contacts, Driving, or Stealth. Skills you already have are left out of the picker; if too few remain, it also offers other skills from the same Ghostwire groups.

Starting resources: no Renown or ¥ from the Profession itself. A Director may grant a small ¥ bonus (for example ¥500) as liquid cash — never as skills, perks, or other character-power budget.

RigTech.Name: Rig-Tech
RigTech.Description:
You maintained and flew drones and remote vehicles for a delivery firm, a security company, or a salvage crew, jacked into the rig.

Skills: you gain Rigging, and choose two of Electronics, Repair, Driving, or Piloting. Skills you already have are left out of the picker; if too few remain, it also offers other skills from the same Ghostwire groups.

Starting resources: no Renown or ¥ from the Profession itself. A Director may grant a small ¥ bonus (for example ¥500) as liquid cash — never as skills, perks, or other character-power budget.

DeckJockey.Name: Deck Jockey
DeckJockey.Description:
You made a living in the Wired: freelance intrusion work, data brokering, or corp pen-testing. You built your own deck and you know how the network actually thinks.

Skills: you gain Hacking, and choose two of Matrix Theory, Electronics, Security Systems, or Streetwise. Skills you already have are left out of the picker; if too few remain, it also offers other skills from the same Ghostwire groups.

Starting resources: no Renown or ¥ from the Profession itself. A Director may grant a small ¥ bonus (for example ¥500) as liquid cash — never as skills, perks, or other character-power budget.

Entertainer.Name: Entertainer
Entertainer.Description:
You performed for a living — club stages, simstim streams, or street-corner shows. You know how to work a crowd and how to be whoever the audience wants.

Skills: you gain Performance, and choose two of Persuasion, Deception, Insight, or Contacts. Skills you already have are left out of the picker; if too few remain, it also offers other skills from the same Ghostwire groups.

Starting resources: no Renown or ¥ from the Profession itself. A Director may grant a small ¥ bonus (for example ¥500) as liquid cash — never as skills, perks, or other character-power budget.

BeatReporter.Name: Beat Reporter
BeatReporter.Description:
You chased stories for a newsfeed until one got too close to a corp that didn’t want it told. You notice details, you know how companies hide things, and you have sources everywhere.

Skills: you gain Perception, and choose two of Corporate, Contacts, Insight, or Electronics. Skills you already have are left out of the picker; if too few remain, it also offers other skills from the same Ghostwire groups.

Starting resources: no Renown or ¥ from the Profession itself. A Director may grant a small ¥ bonus (for example ¥500) as liquid cash — never as skills, perks, or other character-power budget.

Hauler.Name: Hauler / Labor
Hauler.Description:
You drove freight rigs, loaded cargo, or worked heavy labor crews. Hard work, long hauls, and keeping old trucks alive.

Skills: you gain Athletics, and choose two of Driving, Repair, Brawl, or Engineering. Skills you already have are left out of the picker; if too few remain, it also offers other skills from the same Ghostwire groups.

Starting resources: no Renown or ¥ from the Profession itself. A Director may grant a small ¥ bonus (for example ¥500) as liquid cash — never as skills, perks, or other character-power budget.

MercRecruit.Name: Merc Recruit
MercRecruit.Description:
You signed with a private military company or a free company and did a tour in someone else’s war zone. You learned to shoot, march, and survive in the field.

Skills: you gain Firearms, and choose two of Athletics, Survival, Melee, or Heavy Weapons. Skills you already have are left out of the picker; if too few remain, it also offers other skills from the same Ghostwire groups.

Starting resources: no Renown or ¥ from the Profession itself. A Director may grant a small ¥ bonus (for example ¥500) as liquid cash — never as skills, perks, or other character-power budget.

Acolyte.Name: Acolyte
Acolyte.Description:
You served an order of the Light (or a less reputable faith) — rites, exorcisms, and the long nights listening to people confess what they’d seen in the dark.

Skills: you gain Occult, and choose two of Religion, Insight, Warding, or Rituals. Skills you already have are left out of the picker; if too few remain, it also offers other skills from the same Ghostwire groups.

Starting resources: no Renown or ¥ from the Profession itself. A Director may grant a small ¥ bonus (for example ¥500) as liquid cash — never as skills, perks, or other character-power budget.

ChopDocAssistant.Name: Chop-Doc Assistant
ChopDocAssistant.Description:
You assisted a black-clinic chop-doc: holding patients down, sterilizing salvaged chrome, and knowing which gang would pay for which part.

Skills: you gain Cybertech, and choose two of Medicine, Streetwise, Demolitions, or Electronics. Skills you already have are left out of the picker; if too few remain, it also offers other skills from the same Ghostwire groups.

Starting resources: no Renown or ¥ from the Profession itself. A Director may grant a small ¥ bonus (for example ¥500) as liquid cash — never as skills, perks, or other character-power budget.

PureHuman.Name: Pure Human
PureHuman.Description:
Baseline humanity — adaptable, balanced, widely compatible. The default point of comparison.

Pure Human Traits

Signature Trait: @UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.PBCgnAAsXDXQYBnK]{Detect the Supernatural}

Purchased Pure Human Traits

You have 3 ancestry points to spend on the following traits. (Quick Build: Perseverance, Staying Power.)

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.IKlIxTf6cZBswcDp]{Can’t Take Hold (1 Point)}

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.BRyUSHVG9fjDwjRo]{Determination (2 Points)}

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.GLkKrRMeWpCMQD88]{Perseverance (1 Point)}

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.XltgAaOrbUeRoX36]{Resist the Unnatural (1 Point)}

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.b7PH3aCTK3kMDiqA]{Staying Power (2 Points)}

PurchasedTraits.Name: Purchased Traits
PurchasedTraits.Description: You have 3 ancestry points to spend on the following traits. (Quick Build: Perseverance, Staying Power.)

CantTakeHold.Name: Can’t Take Hold
CantTakeHold.Description: Your connection to the natural world allows you to resist certain supernatural effects. You ignore temporary difficult terrain created by magic and psionic abilities. Additionally, when you are force moved by a magic or psionic ability, you can reduce the forced movement distance by 1.

Determination.Name: Determination
Determination.Description: A tolerance for pain and distress allows you to push through difficult situations. If you are frightened, slowed, or weakened, you can use a maneuver to immediately end one of those conditions.

Perseverance.Name: Perseverance
Perseverance.Description: Giving up is for other people. You gain an edge on tests made using the Athletics skill when endurance is what’s being tested. Additionally, when you are slowed, your speed is reduced to 3 instead of 2.
Perseverance.EffectDescription: You gain an edge on tests made using the Athletics skill when endurance is what’s being tested. Additionally, when you are slowed, your speed is reduced to 3 instead of 2.

ResistTheUnnatural.Name: Resist the Unnatural
ResistTheUnnatural.Description: Your instinctive resilience protects you from injuries beyond the routine. Whenever you take damage that isn’t untyped, you can use a triggered action to take half the damage.
ResistTheUnnatural.Trigger: You take damage that isn’t untyped

StayingPower.Name: Staying Power
StayingPower.Description: Your human physiology allows you to fight, run, and stay awake longer than others. You increase your number of Recoveries by 2.

DetectTheSupernatural.Name: Detect the Supernatural
DetectTheSupernatural.Description: As a maneuver, you can open your awareness to detect supernatural creatures and phenomena. Until the end of your next turn, you know the location of any supernatural object, or any undead, construct, or creature from another world within 5 squares, even if you don’t have line of effect to that object or creature. You know if you’re detecting an item or a creature, and you know the nature of any creature you detect.

Corran.Name: Corran
Corran.Description:
The engineered underclass — short, sturdy, unbreakable, and done being looked down on.

Corran Traits

Signature Trait: @UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.ba1Y2sMZbvtNYExs]{Labor Brand}

Purchased Corran Traits

You have 3 ancestry points to spend on the following traits. (Quick Build: Grounded, Hardened Hide.)

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.habR3HLaizrL2bqS]{Great Fortitude (2 Points)}

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.QK9VmXg8GMSAihLL]{Grounded (1 Point)}

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.NkjLgRzuwa9AMGyt]{Hardened Hide (2 Points)}

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.jiUO0B9qZWmoD300]{Stand Tough (1 Point)}

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.C5BuTGq5er1JPPcS]{Stone Shaper (1 Point)}

PurchasedTraits.Name: Purchased Traits
PurchasedTraits.Description: You have 3 ancestry points to spend on the following traits. (Quick Build: Grounded, Hardened Hide.)

LaborBrand.Name: Labor Brand
LaborBrand.Description:
You can carve a brand or rune onto your skin with 10 uninterrupted minutes of work, activated by the engineered resilience in your body. The brand you carve determines the benefit, chosen from:

Detection: Pick a specific type of creature (such as Corran or Goliar) or object (such as gems or medkits). Your brand glows softly when you are within 20 squares of any creature or object of that type, even if you don’t have line of effect. You can change the type of creature or object as a maneuver.

Light: Your skin sheds light for 10 squares. You can turn this light on and off as a maneuver.

Voice: As a maneuver, you can communicate telepathically with a willing creature you have met before and who is within 1 mile of you. You must know the creature’s name, and they must speak and understand a language you know. You and the creature can respond as if having a spoken conversation. You can communicate with a different creature by changing the brand.

You can have one brand active at a time, and can change or remove a brand with 10 uninterrupted minutes of work.
LaborBrand.LightEffectDescription: Your skin sheds light for 10 squares. You can turn this light on and off as a maneuver.

GreatFortitude.Name: Great Fortitude
GreatFortitude.Description: Your hearty constitution prevents you from losing strength. You can’t be made weakened.

Grounded.Name: Grounded
Grounded.Description: Your dense frame and connection to the work make it difficult for others to move you. You have a +1 bonus to stability.

HardenedHide.Name: Hardened Hide
HardenedHide.Description: Your engineered skin affords potent protection. You have a +6 bonus to Stamina, and that bonus increases by 6 at 4th, 7th, and 10th levels.

StandTough.Name: Stand Tough
StandTough.Description: Your body is made to withstand the blows of your enemies. Your Physique score is treated as 1 higher for the purpose of resisting potencies, and you gain an edge on Physique tests when called for to resist environmental effects or a creature’s traits or abilities.

StoneShaper.Name: Stone Shaper
StoneShaper.Description: When you spend 1 uninterrupted hour singing or working, you can reshape any unworked mundane stone within 3 squares. You can’t destroy this stone, but you can move each square of it anywhere within 3 squares, piling it off to one side to dig a hole or building it up to create a wall.

Elvani.Name: Elvani
Elvani.Description:
The engineered aristocracy — beautiful, poised, quick, and effortlessly above you.

Elvani Traits

Signature Trait: @UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.QjFD2vrzmuFFr47T]{Corp Glamor}

Purchased Elvani Traits

You have 3 ancestry points to spend on the following traits. (Quick Build: High Senses, Otherworldly Grace.)

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.BkApfnE52q6O7XBb]{Glamor of Terror (2 Points)}

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.CLe3qQ18f2lUheyp]{Graceful Retreat (1 Point)}

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.pTMx0vJGcnvmQlB0]{High Senses (1 Point)}

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.ApeGL1aixrw7aRUP]{Otherworldly Grace (2 Points)}

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.6VKm9YiHiWS0CPER]{Revisit Memory (1 Point)}

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.H6bwZLNUhvVENjab]{Unstoppable Mind (2 Points)}

PurchasedTraits.Name: Purchased Traits
PurchasedTraits.Description: You have 3 ancestry points to spend on the following traits. (Quick Build: High Senses, Otherworldly Grace.)

CorpGlamor.Name: Corp Glamor
CorpGlamor.Description: A carefully cultivated presence makes others perceive you as interesting and engaging, granting you an edge on Persona tests using the Persuasion skill. This glamor makes you appear and sound slightly different to each creature you meet, since what is engaging to one might be different for another. However, you never appear to be anyone other than yourself.

GlamorOfTerror.Name: Glamor of Terror
GlamorOfTerror.Description: When a foe strikes, you reverse the magic of your glamor to instill fear into their heart. Whenever you take damage from a creature, you can use a triggered action to make that creature frightened of you until the end of their next turn.

GracefulRetreat.Name: Graceful Retreat
GracefulRetreat.Description: You gain a +1 bonus to the distance you can shift when you take the Disengage move action.

HighSenses.Name: High Senses
HighSenses.Description: Your senses are especially keen and perceptive. You gain an edge on tests made to notice threats.

OtherworldlyGrace.Name: Otherworldly Grace
OtherworldlyGrace.Description: Your engineered body and mind can’t be contained for long. Whenever you make a saving throw, you succeed on a roll of 5 or higher.

RevisitMemory.Name: Revisit Memory
RevisitMemory.Description: Accessing memories is as easy as living in the present for you. You gain an edge on tests made to recall lore.

UnstoppableMind.Name: Unstoppable Mind
UnstoppableMind.Description: Your mind allows you to maintain your focus in any situation. You can’t be made dazed.

Goliar.Name: Goliar
Goliar.Description:
The engineered heavy — towering, crushing, and impossible to ignore.

Goliar Traits

Signature Trait: @UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.UsFQr3y8rzouYwYc]{Relentless}

Purchased Goliar Traits

You have 3 ancestry points to spend on the following traits. (Quick Build: Glowing Recovery, Grounded.)

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.4ouhc5JKDMhvC0U8]{Glowing Recovery (2 Points)}

PurchasedTraits.Name: Purchased Traits
PurchasedTraits.Description: You have 3 ancestry points to spend on the following traits. (Quick Build: Glowing Recovery, Grounded.)

Relentless.Name: Relentless
Relentless.Description: Whenever a creature deals damage to you that leaves you dying, you can make a free strike against any creature. If that creature is reduced to 0 Stamina by your strike, you can spend a Recovery.

BloodfireRush.Name: Bloodfire Rush
BloodfireRush.Description:
The engineered fire in your veins makes you run faster in the heat of battle. The first time in any combat round that you take damage, you gain a +2 bonus to speed until the end of the round.

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.gGW48sXk6lvWf9ZW.ActiveEffect.NVGTtYA1twMvPbnS]
BloodfireRush.EffectDescription: The engineered fire in your veins makes you run faster in the heat of battle. The first time in any combat round that you take damage, you gain a +2 bonus to speed until the end of the round.

GlowingRecovery.Name: Glowing Recovery
GlowingRecovery.Description: Your bloodfire allows you to regain your strength quicker than others. Whenever you use the Catch Breath maneuver, you can spend as many Recoveries as you like.

Grounded.Name: Grounded
Grounded.Description: The density of your frame makes it difficult for others to move you. You have a +1 bonus to stability.

Nonstop.Name: Nonstop
Nonstop.Description: Your bloodfire supplies you with a constant rush of adrenaline. You can’t be made slowed.

PassionateArtisan.Name: Passionate Artisan
PassionateArtisan.Description: When you are stirred by a passion for creation, your bloodfire lets you work longer and harder. When you gain your initial skills from your career, culture, class, or other source, choose two skills from the crafting skill group, whether you have those skills or not. Whenever you make a project roll for a crafting project that uses these skills, you gain a +2 bonus to the roll.

Changer.Name: Changer
Changer.Description:
A were-blooded shapeshifter who walks as a human, fights as a hybrid war-beast, and runs as a true animal.

Lineage (required)

Pick one lineage at creation. It is always on and stays on your sheet as a feature: @UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.liCuEIuHFCtAZwzi]{Raven} (Walk + Fly), @UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.L5Fj6nVEju6s361I]{Rat} (size 1S), or @UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.7KRwCZ8xwI2nuOhI]{Wolf} (+2 speed).

Forms

Every Changer gains @UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.qhrDc59fcOPiaNMh]{Changer Forms}: Human, Hybrid (War), and Beast. Changing form is a maneuver, and exactly one form is active at a time. You start in Human Form.

Changer Traits

Changer heroes have access to the following traits.

Signature Trait: @UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.GvoBzKeb871MArtN]{Beast-Hide}

Purchased Changer Traits

You have 3 ancestry points to spend on the following traits. (Quick Build: Savage Burst, Layered Hide.)

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.yw3LAnJVKy0R4PS1]{Pack Guard (1 Point)}

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.AnY2ro2slwfNEZSc]{Feral Cry (2 Points)}

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.SZT2y1ndFs2vR5IG]{Savage Burst (2 Points)}

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.fvEbDEwHmBGxLc4A]{Layered Hide (1 Point)}

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.IeVv5koMNTrHIJn8]{Beast’s Resolve (1 Point)}

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.2c4zUgqqgULDY4WR]{Beast Movement (2 Points)}

PurchasedTraits.Name: Purchased Traits
PurchasedTraits.Description: You have 3 ancestry points to spend on the following traits. (Quick Build: Savage Burst, Layered Hide.)

Lineage.Name: Lineage (required)
Lineage.Description: Choose exactly one lineage: Raven, Rat, or Wolf. Your lineage is always on. Don’t confirm character creation without choosing one.

BeastHide.Name: Beast-Hide
BeastHide.Description: Your hardened hide, fur, or feathers grant you damage immunity equal to [[lookup @level]]{your level} to one of the following damage types: acid, cold, corruption, fire, lightning, or poison. You can change your immunity type when you finish a respite.

PackGuard.Name: Pack Guard
PackGuard.Description: Whenever you or an adjacent creature takes damage from a strike, you can use a triggered action to guard against the blow. You reduce any damage from the strike by an [[/heal @level]]{amount equal to your level}.

FeralCry.Name: Feral Cry
FeralCry.Story: You let loose a piercing shriek, chittering screech, or bone-deep howl to shake your foes’ spirits.

SavageBurst.Name: Savage Burst
SavageBurst.Story: A battering downdraft, a filthy venomous lunge, or a rending pounce tears into your foes.
SavageBurst.Effect: You choose the ability’s damage type from acid, cold, corruption, fire, lightning, or poison.

LayeredHide.Name: Layered Hide
LayeredHide.Description: Select one damage immunity granted by your Beast-Hide trait. You always have this immunity, in addition to the immunity granted by Beast-Hide.

BeastsResolve.Name: Beast’s Resolve
BeastsResolve.Description: As a maneuver, you can recite your resolve. Until the start of your next turn, whenever you make a saving throw, you succeed on a 4 or higher.
BeastsResolve.EffectDescription: Until the start of your next turn, whenever you make a saving throw, you succeed on a 4 or higher.

BeastMovement.Name: Beast Movement
BeastMovement.Description: You can move as your lineage flies or bounds. Raven: true flight. Rat/Wolf: prodigious leaping and climbing bounds. Either way, you can stay aloft for a number of rounds equal to [[lookup formula="max(@M, 1)" evaluate=true]]{your Physique score (minimum 1 round)} before you come down. While moving this way at 3rd level or lower, you have damage weakness 5.
BeastMovement.Director: Two active effects are included in this trait: one for heroes in echelon 1, another for echelon 2+. Players should keep the one that applies.
BeastMovement.Echelon1Description: While moving this way, you can stay aloft for a number of rounds equal to [[lookup @M]]{your Physique score} (minimum 1 round) before you come down. At 3rd level or lower, you have damage weakness 5 while doing so.
BeastMovement.Echelon2Description: While moving this way, you can stay aloft for a number of rounds equal to [[lookup @M]]{your Physique score} (minimum 1 round) before you come down.

Raven.Name: Raven Lineage
Raven.Description:
Cunning, aerial, uncanny. Your movement types are Walk and Fly.

Your Beast-Hide reads as oily black feathers with an iridescent sheen. Your Feral Cry is a piercing shriek and your Savage Burst a battering downdraft of wings and beak. In Beast Form you are a raven.
Raven.EffectDescription: Your movement types are Walk and Fly.

Rat.Name: Rat Lineage
Rat.Description:
Fast, resilient, swarming. Your size is 1S.

Your Beast-Hide reads as matted grey fur, scarred and tough. Your Feral Cry is a chittering screech and your Savage Burst a filthy, venomous lunge. In Beast Form you are a rat.

Wolf.Name: Wolf Lineage
Wolf.Description:
Ferocious, pack-minded, direct. You gain a +2 bonus to speed.

Your Beast-Hide reads as a thick pelt with bristling hackles. Your Feral Cry is a bone-deep howl and your Savage Burst a rending pounce. In Beast Form you are a wolf.

Forms.Name: Changer Forms
Forms.Description:
You have three forms. Changing form is a maneuver. Exactly one form is active at a time, and you start in Human Form.

Human Form: You gain an edge on tests to pass as or blend in among baseline humans. You show no obvious beast tells.

Hybrid (War) Form: You gain an edge on Intimidation tests, and your melee free strikes deal +1 damage. You are visibly a war-beast and can’t pass as human.

Beast Form: You gain an edge on Stealth and Perception tests. You can’t use manufactured weapons, and you can’t speak clear language (growls and body language only).

In Foundry: enable the matching form effect on the Effects tab when you change form; enabling one form turns the others off.

Human.Name: Form: Human
Human.Description: You gain an edge on tests to pass as or blend in among baseline humans (not automated — apply the edge when the test calls for it). You show no obvious beast tells.

Hybrid.Name: Form: Hybrid
Hybrid.Description: You gain an edge on Intimidation tests (automated). Your melee free strikes deal +1 damage (not automated — add it to the roll). You are visibly a war-beast and can’t pass as human.

Beast.Name: Form: Beast
Beast.Description: You gain an edge on Stealth and Perception tests (automated). You can’t use manufactured weapons, and you can’t speak clear language (growls and body language only).

Warnings.MissingLineage: {name} is a Changer without a Lineage. Open the Changer ancestry, find the Lineage advancement, and reconfigure it to choose Raven, Rat, or Wolf.

Mutant.Name: Mutant
Mutant.Description:
Powerful, unstable, endlessly customizable — human clay reshaped by the Dark One’s touch.

Humans whose flesh has been rewritten — inherited taint, corrupted-zone exposure, magical accident, infernal bargain, or corp gene-forging. Born or made carries no mechanical difference. They are the People most directly marked by the cosmic war: living proof the Dark One’s touch can remake baseline humanity into something else.

Mutant Traits

Signature Trait: @UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.dzbVd5iIaHGBULBC]{Aberrant Rapport}

Purchased Mutant Traits

You have 3 ancestry points to spend on the following traits. (Quick Build: Warped Legs, Ossified Crown.)

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.oSFPoMJn8orsYLUY]{Barbed Mutation (1 Point)}

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.ukswcD6uWCcwIg62]{Warped Legs (1 Point)}

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.LM0o1d9TaqZDjhU4]{Taint Flare (1 Point)}

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.CQ1T0rjR6SbKe4VO]{Taint Sight (1 Point)}

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.7xCzjYKMltkS2PiM]{Ossified Crown (2 Points)}

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.9MFaJjqNH5uGtN2s]{Prehensile Mutation (2 Points)}

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.a5qD9riHweABLtJO]{Membrane Wings (2 Points)}

Corruptive Flaw (optional)

At creation you can pick a cosmetic Corruptive Flaw, such as Visible Taint, Hungering Cells, Unstable Form, Taint Sink, or Fractured Mind. It costs no ancestry points and has no mechanical effect: it is color for tells, roleplay, and scenes. There is no Corruption Load meter.

PurchasedTraits.Name: Purchased Traits
PurchasedTraits.Description: You have 3 ancestry points to spend on the following traits. (Quick Build: Warped Legs, Ossified Crown.)

AberrantRapport.Name: Aberrant Rapport
AberrantRapport.Description: Your taint twists how your words and presence are read, giving you a better read on people and a way to steer them. You have one skill of your choice from the social skill group, and you gain an edge on tests when attempting to discover an NPC’s motivations and pitfalls during a negotiation.

BarbedMutation.Name: Barbed Mutation
BarbedMutation.Description: A barbed spur, spine, or tendril punctuates your strikes. Once per round when you make a melee strike, you can deal extra damage with the strike equal to [[/damage max(@M,@A,@R,@I,@P)]]{your highest characteristic score}.

WarpedLegs.Name: Warped Legs
WarpedLegs.Description: Your mutated legs make you faster. You have speed 6.
WarpedLegs.EffectDescription: Your mutated legs make you faster. You have speed 6.

TaintFlare.Name: Taint Flare
TaintFlare.Description:
When your taint flares under stress, it lashes back. Whenever you take damage from a creature, you can use a triggered action to deal that creature psychic damage equal to [[/damage 1d10+@level type=psychic]]{1d10 + your level}.

@UUID[Compendium.draw-steel-ghostwire.origins.Item.91UYvxXgCyETqxIh]{Taint Flare}

TaintFlareAbility.Name: Taint Flare
TaintFlareAbility.Story: Your taint flares under stress and lashes back.
TaintFlareAbility.Effect: You deal [[/damage 1d10+@level type=psychic]]{1d10 + your level psychic damage} to that creature.

TaintSight.Name: Taint Sight
TaintSight.Description: Mutated eyes see through darkness, fog, and other obscuring effects. You don’t take a bane on strikes made against creatures with concealment.

OssifiedCrown.Name: Ossified Crown
OssifiedCrown.Description: Bone plates, horn-like growths, or a hardened cranial ridge mark your force of will. Whenever you make a saving throw, you succeed on a roll of 5 or higher.
OssifiedCrown.EffectDescription: Whenever you make a saving throw, you succeed on a roll of 5 or higher.

PrehensileMutation.Name: Prehensile Mutation
PrehensileMutation.Description: A prehensile tendril, extra limb, or living appendage lets you challenge foes on all sides. You can’t be flanked.

MembraneWings.Name: Membrane Wings
MembraneWings.Description:
Patagia, bone-and-skin wings, or similar membranes are strong enough to take you airborne. While using them to fly, you can stay aloft for a number of rounds equal to [[lookup formula="max(@M, 1)" evaluate=true]]{your Physique score (minimum 1 round)} before you fall. While flying at 3rd level or lower, you have damage weakness 5.

Enable a Membrane Wings effect on your sheet while you fly: echelon 1 (fly and damage weakness 5) at 3rd level or lower, or echelon 2+ (fly only) from 4th level.
MembraneWings.Echelon1Description: You fly. While flying at 3rd level or lower, you have damage weakness 5. You can stay aloft for a number of rounds equal to your Physique score (minimum 1 round) before you fall.
MembraneWings.Echelon2Description: You fly. You can stay aloft for a number of rounds equal to your Physique score (minimum 1 round) before you fall.

Cyborg.Name: Cyborg
Cyborg.Description:
Machine-first threshold beings — integrated, augmented, existentially unstable. Distinct from chrome-augmented meat.

A Cyborg is the far end of the chrome spectrum: effectively all organic Body Integrity spent, frame and cortex first. Living, non-Cyborg heroes who want implants use the Chrome chapter; the Cyborg does not. Full conversion is made, not bred — surgery, battlefield salvage, corp programs, or voluntary upload into a shell.

Hard Constraints

Arcane Severance: You can’t use Magic-keyword abilities. You are barred from the Elementalist and Street Priest classes, and from any Veil-casting path that requires Magic. The Tech-keyword Installed Suite abilities from this ancestry are allowed. You can still be targeted, harmed, or protected by magic.

Tech-only recovery: You are healed by tech, Wrench-style repair, or Medic tech procedures as your table defines, not by Magic healing (Director’s call on Troubadour-style and similar effects).

System Crisis: When you would die under the usual 0 Stamina and dying rules, you instead enter a Director-facing System Crisis (machine failure) rather than a normal organic death spiral. This is a rule pointer only; the full Crisis table isn’t defined yet.

These are Ghostwire chargen and setting rules. They cost no ancestry points. Cyborgs don’t use the Chrome / Body Integrity chapter.

PenetrationOptics.Description:

PredictiveSensors.Name: Predictive Sensors
PredictiveSensors.Description: Your sensors automatically know the location of concealed (not hidden) creatures within 20 squares, and you negate the bane on strikes against them. When you are targeted by a strike, you can use a triggered action to impose a bane on the power roll.

AuxiliaryLimbsAthletics.Name: Auxiliary Limbs — Athletics
AuxiliaryLimbsAthletics.Description: You gain an edge on Athletics and Acrobatics tests when you can use all your limbs.

AuxiliaryLimbsCombat.Name: Auxiliary Limbs — Combat
AuxiliaryLimbsCombat.Description: When you use Grab or Knockback against an adjacent creature, you can target one additional adjacent creature, using the same power roll for both. You can have up to two creatures grabbed at once.

ToughButWithered.Name: Tough But Withered
ToughButWithered.Description:
Your undead body grants you immunity to cold, corruption, lightning, and poison damage equal to [[lookup @level]]{your level}, but you have fire weakness 5. You can’t suffocate, and you don’t need to eat or drink to stay alive.

Additionally, when your Stamina reaches the negative of your winded value, you become inert instead of dying. You fall prone and can’t stand. You continue to observe your surroundings, but you can’t speak, take main actions, maneuvers, move actions, or triggered actions. While inert this way, if you take any fire damage, your body is destroyed and you die. Otherwise, after 12 hours, you [[/heal @recoveries.recoveryValue]]{regain Stamina} equal to your recovery value.

Bloodless.Name: Bloodless
Bloodless.Description: For you, an open wound is indistinguishable from a scratch. You can’t be made bleeding even while dying.

PreviousLife1.AdvancementDescription: Pick one 1-point purchased trait from your Former Life People. Traits from other Peoples are disabled. If every option is disabled, configure Former Life first.

PreviousLife2.AdvancementDescription: Pick one 2-point purchased trait from your Former Life People. Traits from other Peoples are disabled. If every option is disabled, configure Former Life first.

UndeadInfluence.Name: Undead Influence
UndeadInfluence.Description: Your supernatural gifts allow you to influence other undead. You gain an edge on Logic, Instinct, and Persona tests made to interact with undead creatures.

VengeanceMark.Name: Vengeance Mark
VengeanceMark.Description:
As a maneuver, you place a magic sigil on a creature within 10 squares. When you place a sigil, you decide where it appears on the creature’s body, and whether the sigil is visible to only you or to all creatures.

You always know the direction to the exact location of a creature who bears one of your sigils and is on the same world. You can have a number of active sigils equal to [[lookup @level]]{your level}, and can remove a sigil from a creature at will (no action required). If you already have the maximum number of sigils activated and you place a new one, your oldest sigil disappears with no other effect.

Additionally, you have the following signature ability. Signature abilities can be used at will.
